title: Single-cell approach dissecting agr quorum sensing dynamics in Staphylococcus aureus.
authors: Bar, Julian; Pivard, Mariane; Charlton, Samuel G V; Kempchinsky, Andrew G; Gomez-Mejia, Alejandro; Ugolini, Giovanni Stefano; Mairpady Shambat, Srikanth; Secchi, Eleonora; Zinkernagel, Annelies S
one_liner_zh: 该文研究金黄色葡萄球菌agr群体感应系统的单细胞动态，聚焦细菌信号传导而非蛋白质-DNA互作，无AI/物理模拟结合建模，与本课题无关。
abstract: Quorum sensing (QS) enables bacteria to coordinate collective behaviors by secreting and sensing diffusible signals. Understanding QS at single-cell resolution is essential because population-level measurements often obscure regulatory heterogeneity. In Staphylococcus aureus, the accessory gene regulator (agr) system is a major QS-controlled virulence regulator activated by autoinducing peptides (AIPs). Four agr-types exist, each defined by distinct AIPs and capable of cross-inhibition, yet their activation dynamics and interaction hierarchies remain poorly understood. Using microfluidics, time-lapse microscopy, and deep-learning-based image analysis, we quantified agr-activation in congenic and native agr-type strains. Agr-types differed in sensitivity to their homologous AIPs: agr-III was largely unresponsive, whereas agr-IV was highly sensitive with elevated basal activation. Agr-activation distribution was frequently bimodal (simultaneous existence of agr-ON and agr-OFF cells), driven by subpopulations that never activated or switched to agr-OFF despite constant stimulation. Combining homologous and heterologous AIPs, AIP‑IV suppressed pre‑activated agr-I, while AIP-I had no inhibitory effect on agr‑IV, indicating asymmetric cross‑inhibition. In spatially segregated cocultures, diffusional crosstalk resulted in four reproducible agr-interaction regimes, stable-dominance, stable-, delayed-, or unstable-dual-activation, determined by agr-type pairing and influenced by genetic background. Our approach links single-cell signaling to population outcomes and uncovers agr-type-specific asymmetries with potential consequences for strain competition and virulence.
abstract_zh: 群体感应（quorum sensing, QS）使细菌能够通过分泌和感知可扩散信号来协调集体行为。在单细胞分辨率下理解QS至关重要，因为群体水平的测量往往掩盖了调控异质性。在金黄色葡萄球菌（*Staphylococcus aureus*）中，附属基因调节子（accessory gene regulator, agr）系统是主要的QS调控毒力调节因子，由自诱导肽（autoinducing peptides, AIPs）激活。存在四种agr型，每种由不同的AIPs定义，并能相互抑制，然而它们的激活动态和相互作用层级仍知之甚少。利用微流控、延时显微镜和基于深度学习的图像分析，我们量化了同源和天然agr型菌株中的agr激活。agr型对其同源AIP的敏感性不同：agr-III基本无响应，而agr-IV高度敏感且基础激活水平升高。agr激活分布常呈双峰（agr-ON和agr-OFF细胞同时存在），由从未激活或在持续刺激下切换至agr-OFF的亚群驱动。结合同源和异源AIP，AIP-IV抑制了预激活的agr-I，而AIP-I对agr-IV无抑制作用，表明交叉抑制具有不对称性。在空间分离的共培养中，扩散性串扰导致四种可重复的agr相互作用模式：稳定优势、稳定双激活、延迟双激活或不稳定双激活，这些模式由agr型配对决定，并受遗传背景影响。我们的方法将单细胞信号传导与群体结果联系起来，揭示了agr型特异性的不对称性，这可能对菌株竞争和毒力产生影响。
